description: Team-Based Document Scoping — Add team_access array to documents so agents on a given team only see documents tagged for that team. Enables public docs widgets and support chatbots without leaking business/personal documents. Uses existing Agent.team field as the scoping key.

userStories.title: Document team_access column and migration
userStories.description: As a platform developer, I need a team_access TEXT[] column on the documents table so documents can be scoped to specific agent teams.
acceptanceCriteria: Create migration 043_team_based_document_scoping.sql in orchestrator/core/database/migrations/
ALTER TABLE documents ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS team_access TEXT[] DEFAULT '{}'
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_documents_team_access ON documents USING GIN (team_access)
ALTER TABLE sdk_api_keys ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS team VARCHAR(100)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_agents_team ON agents (team) WHERE team IS NOT NULL
Add team_access = Column(PG_ARRAY(String), default=list) to Document model in orchestrator/core/models/core.py ~line 549
Add team = Column(String(100), nullable=True) to SdkApiKey model in orchestrator/core/models/sdk_api_keys.py
All existing documents have team_access = {} (visible to all) — backward compatible
Migration is idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS on all statements)
userStories.notes: Zero-risk additive migration. No data changes. Filtering rule everywhere: WHERE (team_access = '{}' OR :team IS NULL OR :team = ANY(team_access))

userStories.title: Upload with team_access
userStories.description: As a user uploading a document, I can specify which teams should have access via a team_access parameter.
acceptanceCriteria: Add team_access: Optional[str] = Form(None) to upload endpoint in orchestrator/api/documents.py ~line 107
Parse comma-separated string to List[str], store on document record
Pass team_access to DocumentManager in orchestrator/modules/rag/ingestion/manager.py
Include team_access in S3 Vectors chunk metadata during ingestion
Omitting team_access defaults to [] (all teams see it)
Also update orchestrator/api/knowledge_multimodal.py upload endpoint

userStories.title: RAG filters by agent team
userStories.description: As an agent on the Support team, my RAG retrieval only returns chunks from documents with team_access containing 'Support' or empty team_access.
acceptanceCriteria: Add team: Optional[str] = None parameter to RAGService.retrieve() in orchestrator/modules/rag/service.py ~line 210
Add team parameter to _get_candidates() ~line 697
Over-fetch candidates by 2-3x when team filtering is active
Post-retrieval: query PostgreSQL for document IDs matching team filter using GIN index
Filter candidates to only include allowed document_ids
Empty team_access documents always included (backward compatible)
Agent with team=NULL sees all documents (no filtering)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Post-retrieval filter via PostgreSQL lookup (not vector metadata) so team_access changes take effect immediately without re-indexing

userStories.title: Widget docs API with team scope
userStories.description: As a docs widget, I can search documents filtered by team so I only show support articles to end users.
acceptanceCriteria: Create new file orchestrator/api/widgets/docs.py
POST /api/widget/docs/search — accepts query, limit, team; filters by team_access; returns id, title, snippet, tags
GET /api/widget/docs/{document_id} — team-scoped detail with full content
GET /api/widget/docs/categories — distinct tags from team-scoped documents
All endpoints require widget auth with documents:read permission
Team resolution: auth.team (API key) > body.team (request) > None (all)
Returns 200 with empty results for no matches (not 404)
Register router in orchestrator/api/widgets/router.py
userStories.notes: Separate from existing /api/widget/documents which is a general workspace-wide search
